channel: allcoredevs/_threads/Is there any chance for this EIP_ I
searchText: Actually, there is still a chance to convince the core devs to include the EIP today, but I’m not sure if I’ll be able to attend: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2197 Oh, I see you've already commented there—thank you very much Imo it’s very hard to convince them to include the eip but happy to propose that, I’ll try to join Thank you. I hope you will include these points in the agenda. I am hoping we can negotiate some benefits for the temporary account without necessarily needing to add new opcode: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/arguments-for-ephemeral-accounts-and-implementation-approaches/29524 I mean, to be honest seems very reasonable to me to get refills, then next upgrade we can have an EIP specific for that and get selfdestruct deprecated let's see what the core team thinks but I can't find a reason why moving a very legit and important use case to L2. Not only that, but moving these flows to centralized entities. Doesn't make any sense That's right, you can choose to refactor the SELFDESTRUCT or remove it entirely once a native solution from the protocol becomes available <@968526635735326741> Can you please share the data on selfdestructed contracts mentioned in the call? Also, if you can please share what are the complexity of re-including the gas refill logic mentioned would be great And again stressing on this, not re enabling gas refills for selfdestruct will make ephimeral contracts unreasonably expensive and for at least a year the only alternative is centralized enterprises. I genuinely can't see how this can be aligned with Ethereum values.

excerpts.author: gaxanh
excerpts.content: Actually, there is still a chance to convince the core devs to include the EIP today, but I’m not sure if I’ll be able to attend: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2197

excerpts.content: Oh, I see you've already commented there—thank you very much
